name: Almira Sawyer, dress, cloak and habit making

proprietors.name: Almira Sawyer
proprietors.basis: ADOPTED, NOT MINTED. Almira Sawyer is the reconstructed trade head the resident band's `trade_households` stage drew at dressmaker in the south division (slot trade_households:persons/female/20_29/south/family/trade:dressmaker:030), and that card says itself that the business band adopts these heads rather than minting its own. Here the head is not merely the proprietor of the house — the head IS what bought it, because no count of this class was ever printed to be short of.

locations.basis: A FACE, NOT A PREMISES. The placement rule for a dress making shop kept by a south-division household deals this house onto Dearborn Street; the face is drawn on the seed printed in `reconstruction.seed` from the faces that rule allows, and no lot, roof or coordinate is claimed. T-1195 writes the placement policy with its evidence and T-1199 seats this house on the lot grid.
locations.limit_reason: No source places this house, because no source names it: it exists because the resident band drew a dressmaker the town was short of, and the trade names the house he keeps. The street is the reconstruction's own deal and stops there.

dates.basis: NOTHING DATES THIS HOUSE. The head who keeps it is ordered onto the scene date and to nothing narrower, and a keeping is not an opening; the record claims that the house was trading on 1835-07-01 and nothing about either end.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read yankee: Almira Sawyer (yankee). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A register, directory or deed naming a real dress making shop in the south division in 1835 — that house takes this slot and this record is withdrawn with the head.

trade_head.note: A TRADE HEAD, NOT A SHORTFALL AND NOT A ROOF. The December 1835 State census's eighteen lines never reach this class, so the order book holds no bucket to point at and no count of it can be short; and nothing in data/structures/ is a dress making shop, so there is no committed building to buy the firm either. What IS committed is the man: the resident band drew Almira Sawyer at dressmaker because the 1839 trade table says the town was short of the trade, and the register's one printed house of the trade is Sarah D. Howe's dress, cloak and habit making on Lake Street, and the December census enumerates no dress maker. The house is withdrawn with the head.

basis.note: the resident band drew 1 head(s) at dressmaker in the south division and the register's one printed house of the trade is Sarah D. Howe's dress, cloak and habit making on Lake Street, and the December census enumerates no dress maker. The style is dealt on the seed printed beside it from the period forms the register itself carries: the form the register prints the trade in: 'Sarah D. Howe', the town's one printed dress maker, named in full. The goods line is Sarah D. Howe's trade line whole, as the register prints it.

reconstruction.withdrawn_if: the retirement of the head himself, a re-cut of the order book that no longer orders his person bucket, or a source naming a real house of this class; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
